glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue, starving it of oxygen.
glossary.Occlusion: Complete blockage of a vessel so blood cannot pass.
glossary.Diabetes: Chronically high blood glucose from lack of insulin or insulin resistance.
glossary.Hyperlipidaemia: Raised levels of fats such as cholesterol in the blood.
glossary.Pulseless: No palpable pulse distal to a blockage.
glossary.Numbness: Loss of feeling in part of the body.
glossary.Amputation: Surgical removal of all or part of a limb.
glossary.Oxidative stress: Damage from reactive oxygen species released when oxygen returns to ischaemic tissue.
glossary.Inflammatory mediators: Chemicals such as cytokines that drive inflammation and vessel leak.
glossary.Platelet aggregation: Platelets clumping together to form a plug.
glossary.Occlusive thrombus: A clot that completely blocks the vessel lumen.
glossary.Vascular surgery: Surgical specialty treating diseases of the arteries and veins.
glossary.Potentiate: To increase the effect of something.
glossary.Propagation: Extension of a clot further along a vessel.
glossary.Clotting factors: Blood proteins that work in sequence to form a fibrin clot.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available for confirming a diagnosis.
glossary.Neurological exam: Examination of sensation, power and reflexes.
glossary.Vascular exam: Examination of pulses, colour, temperature and capillary refill.
glossary.Capillary leak: Fluid escaping from damaged small vessels into the tissues.
glossary.Fascial compartment: Group of muscles enclosed by tough fascia that cannot stretch when they swell.
glossary.Irreversible: Cannot be undone; dead tissue does not recover.
